source: Hastie & Pennington (c.1993-94) Implications of the Story Model for the Trial Judge's Behavior (Canadian Institute for the Administration of Justice)
finding: The authors list five things that set a juror's global confidence: coverage, completeness, internal consistency, plausibility, and uniqueness. Uniqueness is defined as how far the juror is entertaining alternative stories, not how many stories exist in the abstract. They also say the side whose evidence follows a narrative order of proof has an advantage.
numbers: No numbers. Footnote 2 lists the empirical sources: Pennington and Hastie 1986 (JPSP 51:242), 1988 (JEP:LMC 14:521), 1991 Cardozo L Rev, 1993 chapters.
quote: if a story lacks uniqueness, that is, there is more than one coherent story, then certainty concerning the accuracy of any one explanation will be lowered
limits: A restatement for judges, not a data paper. Gap 2 (exact numbers from 1986/1988/1992) is NOT closed by this source.
agent_relevance: Uniqueness should be computed over the stories the agent actually generated and kept alive, which is what code can count. Order of presentation (narrative vs witness order) is a separate bias to guard against.

source: Hastie & Pennington (1996) The O.J. Simpson Stories: Behavioral Scientists' Reflections (U. Colorado Law Review 67)
finding: Authors state that coverage and coherence govern which story is accepted, while uniqueness only adds to confidence. Coherence is consistency, plausibility and completeness combined with no stated rule. If one story is coherent it is accepted; if several are, belief in any one is reduced.
quote: two certainty principles govern acceptance: coverage and coherence. An additional certainty principle, uniqueness, will contribute to confidence.
limits: Verbal theory only. It does not say whether a fully covering but inconsistent story beats a partly covering consistent one.
agent_relevance: Confirms K01/K02: any scoring formula is our design. Safe split for code: accept by coverage plus contradiction count, report confidence from the runner-up gap.

source: Attempt to open Pennington & Hastie 1986 (JPSP 51:242), 1988 (JEP:LMC 14:521), 1992 (JPSP 62:189) full text
url: several hosts tried (Cardozo Law Review PDF 404, Semantic Scholar 429, scholar.archive.org bot check, Wiley/APA paywalls)
finding: None of the three founding experiments could be opened in this run, so their verdict percentages, order-effect sizes and confidence-by-uniqueness data are still unrecorded.
limits: Search budget was spent; APIs were rate limited (OpenAlex budget exhausted, arXiv API 429).
agent_relevance: Treat the order-of-evidence and uniqueness-to-confidence findings as secondhand until a later pass opens the papers.

source: Engel & Gloeckner (2013) Role-induced bias in court, J Behav Decis Making 26:272-284 (reporting Simon, Krawczyk, Bleicher & Holyoak 2008, The transience of constructed preferences)
finding: E&G state that coherence effects are transient and fade after some time, citing Simon et al. 2008. They report the role effect on verdict prediction as 14% in their data against 17% in Simon et al. 2008. Simon 2008 itself was not opened.
numbers: Role effect on verdict prediction: 14% (E&G, later study) vs 17% (Simon et al. 2008). Time x role interaction coeff -1.85, z -3.06, p=.002. Short deliberation: role effect p=.003. Long deliberation: p=.66.
limits: The duration of the shift (hours, days) is not given in the pages read. The experiment number for the time split is read from a two-column layout and should be checked.
agent_relevance: Coherence-driven bias is weaker when the decider takes longer. An agent should therefore spend extra steps before committing and should record initial ratings outside the context.

source: Engel & Gloeckner (2013) Role-induced bias in court, Experiment 2 (high incentives)
finding: With a large reward for a correct prediction, role-induced bias still appeared. Bias again fell with deliberation time but the interaction was not significant. Quick deciders were biased, slow deciders were not.
numbers: N=92. Extra payment about 100 euro (about 140 dollars) paid in 1 of 10 cases. Time x role interaction coeff -1.12, z -1.18, p=.24. Quick half p=.003, slow half p=.23.
limits: A median split is a weak test, since the interaction is not significant. Student sample, vignette.
agent_relevance: Money for accuracy does not remove coherence bias; slowing down helps only weakly. Remedies must be structural (store first ratings, rate before choosing).

source: Liu (2026) LLMs as a Jury: Cross-Model Consensus Can Outperform Process Reward Models (arXiv 2607.10139v3)
finding: Best-of-12 selection from Qwen3-235B candidates on seven benchmarks. Agreement among independently trained models beat self-consistency voting and beat a model scoring its own candidates. The single-model verifier captured about none of the gap to an oracle.
numbers: Accuracy (SC / own-LLM-verifier / cross-model consensus / oracle): AIME-24 36.7/30.0/56.7/56.7; AIME-25 33.3/33.3/40.0/43.3; MATH-500 95.2/93.2/96.6/98.6; OlympiadBench 65.4/62.2/72.6/79.1; GPQA 33.3/26.3/35.9/53.0 (n=198); MMLU-Pro 43.8/43.9/46.2/48.9; GSM8K 96.7/95.9/97.2/97.9. Gain over SC up to +20.0 on AIME-24, p=0.001; GPQA +2.6 not significant.
limits: Closed-answer benchmarks only, extra compute for several models, preprint. The gain vanishes when the pool saturates and a shared-error floor limits science tasks (GPQA, MMLU-Pro).
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partly closed. Code-computed agreement across independent runs beats same-model voting and self-judging, but this is cross-model, not a coverage or coherence score. It does not test story scoring itself.

source: Liu (2026) LLMs as a Jury, abstention results
finding: Agreement level works as a confidence dial. A unanimous four-model panel is almost always right, and relaxing to a three-quarters majority keeps most accuracy at higher coverage.
numbers: Unanimous panel: 99.5% correct on MATH-500 while answering 85% of problems; 100% on AIME-2024/2025 unanimous subset; three-quarters majority: 98.5% at 94% coverage. Unanimous accuracy saturates at 0.769 on the science/knowledge sets. Parameter-free law predicts consensus accuracy with mean absolute error 0.028 over seven benchmarks.
limits: Agreement is across models, not a runner-up gap inside one model's story list. Ceiling set by shared misconceptions.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partly closed: an agreement-based uniqueness signal predicts correctness well on math. Use unanimity as an abstain or escalate rule.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation (arXiv 2311.17311)
finding: Asking the LLM to pick the answer most consistent with the other samples works on free-form tasks where voting cannot be applied, and matches voting on math.
numbers: GSM8K gpt-3.5-turbo: SC 78.5 vs USC 77.8; PaLM 2-L: SC 90.4 vs USC 90.2. MATH 37.9 vs 37.4 (PaLM 2-L). TruthfulQA GPT-judge: greedy 62.1, USC 67.7 (PaLM 2-L); greedy 79.8, USC 82.5 (gpt-3.5). Response order effect small across 5 shuffles.
limits: Needs one extra LLM call and all samples in context. The selector is an LLM, not code. Models are 2023 era. Table column-to-model mapping is read from garbled text extraction.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 (open-ended): a model-run consistency selector is the baseline a code-computed coverage and contradiction score must beat at equal tokens. Not yet tested.

source: Mitchell et al. (2022) ConCoRD: Enhancing Self-Consistency of Pre-Trained Language Models through NLI (arXiv 2211.11875)
finding: A weighted MaxSAT solver over the model's own candidate answers and pairwise NLI-estimated entailment and contradiction edges raises accuracy and consistency without retraining.
numbers: BeliefBank F1 +8.1 absolute (Macaw-Large) and about 7 (Macaw-3B); ConVQA accuracy +5.0 (LXMERT); Natural Questions up to 8.7% relative gain over naive baseline. Beat gold-constraint baseline on BeliefBank F1. Gap to oracle remains on NQ. Both entailment and contradiction edges help, often redundantly.
limits: Small models (T5, Macaw, LXMERT, ViLT) and top-2 candidates. No comparison with self-consistency voting and no frontier model. Edge weights come from an NLI model, which is noisy.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: shows noisy NLI edge weights are tolerable for MaxSAT with small models. Still no test against voting at equal tokens on a frontier model.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? (ICLR 2024, arXiv 2306.13063)
finding: Stated (verbalized) confidence is overconfident and a weak failure predictor, even for GPT-4. Agreement among 5 sampled answers is a much better failure predictor on arithmetic.
numbers: GPT-4 vanilla verbalized confidence average AUROC 62.7% (random 50%). GSM8K AUROC rose from 54.8% (verbalized) to 92.7% (5 samples with consistency). Average ECE of GPT-3, GPT-3.5, Vicuna above 0.377. Consistency with M=5 has only 6 possible values.
limits: 2023 models, five datasets, weak on professional-knowledge tasks (law, ethics). Consistency gain is largest on arithmetic.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 largely closed for sampling agreement: agreement across samples predicts correctness far better than the model's own stated confidence. A runner-up-gap measure over generated stories was not tested.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning (arXiv 2203.11171)
finding: The share of sampled decodes that agree with the final answer is highly correlated with accuracy on GSM8K, so low agreement signals low confidence.
numbers: Correlation shown in Figure 5 only, no coefficient in the text.
limits: Plot not numerically reported; PaLM-540B era.
agent_relevance: Supports using the vote margin as the uniqueness signal and as an abstain trigger.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench (arXiv 2306.05685), position bias
finding: LLM judges change their pick when the two answers swap places. Claude-v1 and GPT-3.5 mostly favour the first slot.
numbers: Consistency under swap: Claude-v1 23.8% (75.0% favour first), GPT-3.5 46.2% (50.0% first), GPT-4 65.0% (30.0% first). Agreement with humans above 80% for GPT-4.
limits: Pairwise judging on 2023 models. Newer models were not tested here.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: any LLM-run coverage or plausibility judge needs both orders and a code tie rule.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench, verbosity attack
finding: Padding an answer with a rephrased copy of its own list fools weak judges into rating it better. This is a cheap way to game a coverage or completeness score.
numbers: Failure rate on 23 padded answers: Claude-v1 91.3%, GPT-3.5 91.3%, GPT-4 8.7%. On 10 math questions GPT-4 judge failure 14/20 default, 6/20 chain-of-thought, 3/20 with reference answer.
limits: Small sample (23 answers). One attack type. Identical answers were tied correctly.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 partly closed: padding gamed 2023 judges (91.3%) but not GPT-4 (8.7%). Count coverage in code against a fixed evidence list, not by judge reading length.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (ICLR 2024, arXiv 2310.01798)
finding: Without an outside signal, asking a model to review its own answer does not help and often hurts. With oracle labels it helps a lot, so the gain comes from the external check.
numbers: GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 after two rounds; CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after round one and 41.8 after round two; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 then 89.0. With oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 95.5, GPT-4 97.5. GPT-3.5 keeps its initial GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: Reasoning tasks, 2023 models, no tool access. Table 3 column assignment read from garbled extraction.
agent_relevance: Supports putting selection and checks in code or in a different run, not letting the same context grade its own story (same lesson as d06).

source: Lehr et al. (2025) Kernels of selfhood: GPT-4o shows humanlike cognitive consistency (arXiv 2502.07088), design check for Gap 5
finding: The effects are measured against a control-essay group, not against the model's own earlier rating of the same item. No condition stores an earlier rating outside the chat, so whether external storage removes the shift is untested.
numbers: Study 1: pro-Putin essay vs control d=2.164 (n=50 per cell, t(98)=10.82); anti-Putin d=1.795; choice vs no-choice d=0.981 (pro), d=0.252 (anti), 150 per cell in Study 2.
limits: Attitude toward a person, not ratings of case evidence. One model family plus a Claude 3.5 third-person check.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open for evidence ratings. Effect sizes are large enough that a within-chat before and after test will be easy to detect.

source: Qi & Lerman (2026) Confident but Conflicted: Internal Uncertainty and Cognitive Dissonance Resolution in LLMs (arXiv 2606.22633)
finding: Four LLMs revise a prior stance on health claims depending on the source authority and the evidence quality, and clearly false claims produce near-zero revision. Revision size differs by model and tracks internal uncertainty in two open models.
numbers: Trust Elasticity baseline on clearly false claims: Qwen 0.024, Grok 0.169, Llama 0.264, GPT-4o 0.113. Absolutist minus overstated claims in Llama +0.404. 12 claims, four models. Per-topic backfire up to TE -3.00 (Llama, Keto, Reddit and pilot study).
limits: Health claims, not legal evidence. Not a before and after rating of evidence items.
agent_relevance: How much a model moves after conflicting input depends on model and source cues, so the size of any coherence shift must be measured per model.

source: Dalal et al. (2024) Inference to the Best Explanation in LLMs, search for follow-ups (arXiv 2402.10767; arXiv title search for IBE-Eval)
finding: A search for IBE-Eval on arXiv returns only the original paper (v1 Feb 2024, revised Mar 2025). No replication on current models or open-ended tasks was found in this run.
numbers: Original numbers: up to 77% accuracy, COPA and E-CARE, GPT-3.5 and Llama 2.
limits: One query on the arXiv search page; absence is weak evidence only. Searches for LLM story-model jury papers and mock-jury LLM papers also returned no results.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open. Treat parsimony and hedging as untested on frontier models; test them on our own set before use.
